steps.title: Skill
steps.body: A learned action with a predetermined result that can be reproduced consistently with minimum effort and time. Skills are developed through practice and experience.

steps.title: Ability
steps.body: An innate, inherited trait that underpins skilled performance. Abilities are the building blocks of skills and are largely genetically determined.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Most skills fall somewhere between the two extremes. A netball chest pass is basic, but adding a defender and deciding when to pass makes it more complex. Context matters.

steps.title: Key Principle
steps.body: The more open and externally paced a skill is, the more decision-making is required. Practice should therefore include game-like situations. Closed, self-paced skills can be practised in isolated, repetitive drills.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always give sporting examples when classifying skills - marks depend on application Remember that skills are on a continuum, not either/or - explain where on the continuum Use the terminology precisely: "open/closed continuum" not "open or closed skill type" When asked to classify a skill, use all four continua where possible Link classification to practice type - open skills need variable practice, closed skills need fixed practice Know the difference between skill and ability - this is a common 2-mark question
